title: Topological Sort: Course Schedule
contract: Directed edges [u,v] require u before v. Return whether all n courses can be completed.
brute: boolean[] done=new boolean[n];for(int round=0;round<n;round++){int chosen=-1;for(int v=0;v<n;v++)if(!done[v]){boolean ready=true;for(int[] edge:edges)if(edge[1]==v&&!done[edge[0]])ready=false;if(ready){chosen=v;break;}}if(chosen<0)return false;done[chosen]=true;emit("Scan prerequisites to find one available course","chosen",chosen,"done",done);}return true;
optimal: List<List<Integer>> g=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)g.add(new ArrayList<>());int[] degree=new int[n];for(int[] edge:edges){g.get(edge[0]).add(edge[1]);degree[edge[1]]++;}Deque<Integer> q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)if(degree[i]==0)q.add(i);int processed=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();processed++;for(int v:g.get(u))if(--degree[v]==0)q.add(v);emit("Remove a zero-indegree course","course",u,"remaining indegrees",degree,"ready",q);}return processed==n;
reasoning: Repeatedly scan for a vertex whose prerequisites are all completed; failure before n removals signals a cycle.
Cache unmet-prerequisite counts as indegrees and update only outgoing neighbors after removing a vertex.
Kahn's queue contains exactly currently available courses. Fewer than n processed vertices means a directed cycle, not merely a disconnected graph.
